title: Temporal Equivalence Principle: A Unified Resolution to the JWST High-Redshift Anomalies
abstract:
JWST has revealed a pattern of high-redshift anomalies—such as extreme star formation efficiencies and unexpected stellar-to-dynamical mass ratios—that appear preferentially in deep gravitational potentials. This work tests whether these tensions can be resolved by relaxing the assumption of universal cosmic time. Under the Temporal Equivalence Principle (TEP)—a continuously screened two-metric framework—proper time depends on the local environment in unscreened halos. Using a prespecified magnitude-sector benchmark (κ_gal = 0.960 × 10⁶ mag, Paper 11 — where distinct empirical Cepheid-channel recoveries bracket the benchmark with a midpoint of 0.943 × 10⁶ mag, within 1.8%, and Step 62 derives |κ_P²^pred(λ_0=1)| = 1.196 × 10⁶ mag from the Cepheid envelope density ratio ρ_T/⟨ρ⟩(10 d) = 8.45 × 10⁵ at the unit-transport benchmark λ_0 = 1 with bare coupling |β_A| = 1 fixed by Paper 0, matching the direct SH0ES P²-carrier fit (1.191 ± 0.480) × 10⁶ mag to 0.5% (λ_0 = 0.995 ± 0.401)) applied without any JWST-specific parameter refitting, this framework quantitatively accounts for the leading photometric and kinematic excesses.

To address mass-proxy circularity, the framework is tested against kinematic data using the JWST-SUSPENSE survey (N=15) and a broader velocity dispersion (σ)-based expansion (N=75, Step 171). In the SUSPENSE sample, the dynamical mass-to-light inference response (R_ML) retains residual spectral-age information after controlling for stellar mass and redshift (ρ = +0.556, p = 0.032), whereas stellar mass loses its predictive power once R_ML is controlled (ρ = +0.031, p = 0.91). In the broader N=75 velocity-dispersion expansion, evaluating the purely kinematic predictor R_ML,σ^dir under the Virial-exact depth map Ψ ∝ σ² (with zero dependence on SED-fitted M_* or size Rₑ) yields a strong circularity-free partial correlation controlling for redshift: ρ(R_ML,σ^dir, M_*,obs | z) = +0.463 (p = 2.84 × 10⁻⁵, N=75), strengthening to ρ = +0.608 (p = 8.43 × 10⁻⁷) on the N=55 exact-M_dyn subsample and ρ = +0.575 (p = 0.0080) on the N=20 stellar absorption-line subsample. Under the Virial-exact depth map Ψ ∝ σ², all five physical subsamples (pooled N=75, absorption N=20, emission N=55, z ≥ 4 N=56, and SUSPENSE N=15) agree in residual-z sign (5/5), and holding the local z=0 reference at z_ref=0 (Ψ(σ)√(1+z)-Ψ_ref) yields sign agreement across all three N ≥ 15 individual surveys plus the absorption tracer while attenuating the absorption-line residual-z trend by 86.5% (+0.252 → +0.034).

In large-sample photometry (N = 1,254 across three surveys), dust emergence and apparent evolutionary advance align strongly with potential depth (ρ = +0.635 at z > 8), organizing more cleanly along an effective-time coordinate than raw cosmic time. A secondary photometric test confirms that R_ML carries sSFR information beyond mass and redshift (ρ(R_ML, sSFR | M_*, z) = -0.62, p = 8.2 × 10⁻²⁹), with the negative sign predicted by the TEP measurement equations (sSFR_obs ∝ R_ML^m-n_SPS with m < n_SPS). Furthermore, a nested Bayesian model comparison of the SED observables—utilizing a joint covariance likelihood that accounts for correlated outputs (Steps 176, 179)—shows that the nested augmented model (raw mass + z + log R_ML, 17 parameters, ln Z = -1243.8) is the single highest-evidence model in the canonical ensemble, beating the unconditioned raw mass+z baseline (ln Z = -1248.2) by Δln Z = +4.45 ± 1.09 (BF = 85.4 : 1, >4σ positive evidence for adding log R_ML despite the 4-parameter Occam penalty), while the direction-isolation diagnostic confirms that the R_ML-aligned component carries Δln Z = +55.9 ± 1.0 (lnBF = +41.5 for 9-parameter TEP-only over orthogonalized standard, and lnBF = +9.07 ± 0.93, BF = 8,720 : 1 in symmetric conventional residual space). Finally, the lensing and environmental-channel audit (Step 182) demonstrates that explicitly de-magnifying stellar masses by the UNCOVER DR4 lens magnification μₘₗ sharpens the z>8 dust–R_ML correlation from ρ = +0.646 to ρ = +0.656 (p = 1.30 × 10⁻³², N=254), that the correlation holds in the unmagnified μₘₗ ≤ 1.05 outer field at ρ = +0.603 (p = 1.29 × 10⁻¹⁵, N=144) and strengthens to ρ = +0.667 (p = 1.09 × 10⁻¹⁷, N=127) across sightlines traversing the inner half of the foreground Abell 2744 cluster well (z = 0.308), and that the foreground cluster sightline coordinates (d_A2744, log₁₀μₘₗ) add Δln Z = +26.2 on the 3 physical observables (+34.2 on all 4), consistent with intermediate-path temporal transport along the cluster line of sight (Paper 19), positioning TEP as a coherent and falsifiable organizing framework for high-redshift galaxy evolution.
